title: Fit passenger group rules inside each fold
summary: Compare a sex-group majority baseline with one passenger-class change on identical stratified folds. Generated teaching passengers make the train-only workflow runnable without distributing Titanic data.
environment: Recorded with Python 3.12.14 and its standard library only on Darwin arm64. This local CPU run is the recorded environment; other environments are not covered by this receipt.
steps: Download the script and run with Python 3.12.14. The fixture needs no package installation or account.
Compare both rules on each of the five unchanged folds, then their unweighted average. Group decisions and unseen-group fallback use training labels only.
Explain which folds disagree and whether the class-group change helps consistently. Do not select by repeatedly looking at the same validation labels.
Optional: use --csv authorized-train.csv with PassengerId,Sex,Pclass,Survived. The generated CSV path is tested; actual Titanic data has not been run here.
limitations: Generated fixture is not Titanic data; no leaderboard submission or historical reproduction.
Random stratification does not isolate passenger families.
Aggregate is an unweighted mean of folds, not Kaggle test accuracy.
Memory measures traced Python allocations, not process RSS.
split_definition: Five target-stratified folds with seed 17; each row validates once; group rules fit training rows only.

project.outcome: Compare a sex-group majority baseline with one passenger-class change on identical stratified folds. Generated teaching passengers make the train-only workflow runnable without distributing Titanic data.
prerequisites: Run a Python script locally and read per-split metric results.

access.instructions: Use the generated teaching fixture with --fixture. Optional private inputs require your own authorized access; they have not been verified by this receipt.
access.authorization: Original generated teaching fixture distributed with the script; no competition files required.

project.baseline: Fit sex-majority using training rows only on the fixed declared splits.
project.controlled_change: Compare sex-class-majority on exactly the same splits; a worse metric is a valid outcome.
diagnostics: Inspect every recorded split and compare the direction and size of the method difference.
Explain the split assumption and at least one limit before choosing another experiment.

troubleshooting.recovery: Use the pinned Python version, inspect the script error, and rerun the fixture before attempting authorized private inputs.
